title: G-quadruplex DNA reprograms the photochemistry of CX-5461 toward radical-driven anticancer activity.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: There are no data files to open. The data availability statement says only 'available in the article and in its online supplementary material' — no repository, no accession (Europe PMC text-mining found only a GenBank ID, L34964, and a DOI). I searched Zenodo/Dryad on the article DOI (nothing), checked NCBI links (only the PMC record), and tried the Europe PMC supplementary-file endpoint twice and the NCBI open-access package once; both failed (timeout and HTTP 404), so even the supplementary PDF could not be retrieved. I read the full open-access text (89 kB) and grepped it for tables, deposited data, oligonucleotide sequences, cell lines and dose-response values.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the experiments: that oligonucleotide sequences are listed in Supplementary Table S1, that one further Supplementary Table S2 exists, that measurements are singlet-oxygen quantum yields, fluorescence/absorbance titrations, cell viability with and without light, 8-oxoG and gamma-H2AX staining, and CT26 syngeneic mouse tumour growth. The scale (a handful of DNA sequences, one compound, one main tumour model) is inferred from the methods text, not from a file.

a1_downloadable.note: No dataset is deposited anywhere. The data availability statement points to the article and its supplementary material only; the supplement is publisher-hosted and could not be retrieved (Europe PMC endpoint timed out twice, NCBI open-access package returned 404). Figures in a PDF are not a downloadable dataset.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No label column exists anywhere. Any target (e.g. singlet-oxygen quantum yield, or light-versus-dark potency) would have to be hand-transcribed out of figure panels and a PDF table — construction by inference across sources, which is exactly the A2 failure mode.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs exist only as text: DNA sequences are referenced in Supplementary Table S1 (not retrievable), and the only chemical input is one compound, CX-5461, named rather than given as a machine-readable structure.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are stated carefully in the methods (µM, nM, quantum yield as a dimensionless ratio against phenalenone, mM KCl) — the one Part A item this paper would pass, but it is moot with no file.

a5_enough_rows.note: A single-compound photochemistry and pharmacology study: one ligand, a small number of G-quadruplex-forming oligonucleotides (c-MYC dominates the text, with VEGF and KIT1 mentioned), and one syngeneic mouse model (CT26). The labelled measurements number in the tens, versus the ~1,500-row bar. I could not count them exactly because the supplement is unavailable.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small — but small for the wrong reason: there is almost nothing there.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked at all: there is no download whose counts could be compared with the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: Provenance is clean where measurements exist — real spectroscopy (near-infrared singlet-oxygen phosphorescence at 1270 nm against a phenalenone reference), cell assays and animal experiments, not another model's output. Again moot given A1/A2/A5.

existing_models.name: AGAPE (computAtional G-quadruplex Affinity PrEdiction), a machine-learning workflow that predicts whether a small molecule stabilises a G-quadruplex (a four-stranded DNA fold)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported ~90% accuracy with gradient-boosted trees (XGBoost) plus naive Bayes and random forest in a consensus vote; the split is not described in the preprint abstract I retrieved, so I cannot say whether it was random or grouped by chemical scaffold.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not determined from the abstract alone; I did not retrieve the discussion.

integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: With one compound and a handful of sequences there is nothing to join on; a join would need a G-quadruplex ligand activity table that this paper does not provide.

honest_claim_h3: No model can be trained from this paper; the only honest claim available is a description of what the paper itself measured for one drug.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a drug's structure and a DNA sequence to predict how much light-driven damage the pair produces.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would show a model a small molecule plus a G-quadruplex-forming DNA sequence (a four-stranded DNA fold) and ask how the DNA changes the molecule's light chemistry. This paper supplies roughly one compound and a few sequences — far too few examples; I could not verify an exact count.
plain_idea.predict: Outputs would be the amount of reactive oxygen produced (singlet oxygen quantum yield, measured by infrared light emission at 1270 nm) and the light-versus-dark potency ratio in cells. The true answers come from spectroscopy and cell viability assays described in the methods.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Medicinal chemists designing light-activated cancer drugs would like to know in advance which DNA contexts flip a photosensitiser between damage modes; but answering that needs a table of many compounds, and this paper studies one.

ml_idea: Considered and dropped: predict light-activated reactive-oxygen output and light-versus-dark cytotoxicity for G-quadruplex-binding small molecules. This paper is a deep single-compound mechanism study of CX-5461 (pidnarulex), not a measurement table, so it offers no training rows.

effort.compute_note: No compute estimate is meaningful: there is no dataset. Sizes above reflect the text and a PDF supplement only.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the data availability statement — 'available in the article and in its online supplementary material' with no accession — then count the distinct DNA sequences in the methods. Both take five minutes and both kill it.

verdict_reason: Fails Part A1, A2, A3, A5 and A7: no deposited data, no label column, one compound and a few DNA sequences, nothing downloadable to count.
